concept.name: Volume profile
concept.definition: A charting study that displays, for a specified period, a horizontal histogram of total traded volume at each price level. Unlike the TPO-based Market Profile, which counts time brackets at price, the volume profile counts contracts or shares actually traded at price, revealing where business concentrated and where it was absent.
concept.intuition: It rotates the volume histogram 90 degrees: instead of volume per time bar, you see volume per price — the market's actual footprint of where trading happened.
concept.mechanics: The period's price range is divided into rows; volume from lower-timeframe data (or tick data) is assigned to the row containing its price and summed; the histogram is then rendered with derived levels — point of control (highest-volume row) and value area (rows containing a set percentage, default 70%, of total volume).
concept.failure_modes: Resolution and row-count settings materially change the picture, and on spot forex or CFDs only tick or proxy volume exists; on non-standard chart types (Renko, Heikin Ashi) both price and volume are distorted, as platform documentation warns.
concept.misconceptions: Volume profile is a reactive, backward-looking tool — its own platform documentation stresses it shows what already happened rather than predicting what comes next; high-volume levels are not automatically support or resistance.
concept.example: A session volume profile on ES shows 25% of the day's volume between 4,515 and 4,520 with a POC at 4,517; the next day, price stalls repeatedly in that band on the first retest.
